Treatment transition scenario: DTG for people living with HIV initiating ART

Comments: • Potential risk of neural tube defects among infants exposed to DTG during the conception period • Women not using or accessing contraception or who want to be pregnant can use DTG or EFV based on informed choice of the risks and benefits of each regimen
• Possibility of conception during breastfeeding remains

Preferred approach: Initiate TDF + 3TC + DTG (DTG dose adjustment needed)
Comments: • DTG 50 mg twice daily if rifampicin is being used as the anti-TB regimen

Treatment transition scenario: DTG for people living with HIV already using a first-line ART regimen
Clinical or immune failure or viral load not suppressed
Preferred approach: Switch to AZT + 3TC + DTG or PI/rc
Comments: • No evidence to support the efficacy of DTG when used in combination with an inactive NRTI backbone • Provide adherence support

Preferred approach: Substitution to TDF + 3TC + DTG may be considered according to national recommendations
Comments: • Substitution should be considered in the context of drug supply and patient choice • Substitution may confer new side-effects and interfere with adherence • DTG regimens may be more durable in the long term

Treatment transition scenario: Clinically and immunologically stabled and viral load unknown
Preferred approach: Give priority to viral load testing or consider other programmatic or clinical indications indications for substitution to DTG based ART
Comments: • No evidence to support the efficacy of DTG when used in combination with an inactive NRTI backbone • provide adherence support

Treatment transition scenario: Stabled on suboptimal first-line ART regimens
Comments: • Substitution may confer new side-effects. • Provide adherence support
